To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed new cloning vectors to improve CFP and YYP production in B. subtili and that we used these vectors to visualize differential expression of the abrb and spoIIA promoters in B. subtlis.

the addition of the first eight amino acid residues of the ComGA protein from Bacillus subtili s to the N termini of CFP and YPF improves the production of these fluorescent proteins in B. subtili s by a factor of 20 to 70.
we have improved the production of the cyan and yellow fluorescent protein in the Gram-positive model organism B. subtil is.
In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the fluorescent-protein production in B. subtili and with the application of these proteins in B. subtiilis as a model organism.
the construction of improved fluorescent-protein expression vectors and with the visualization of differential gene expression.

the development of new vectors for the visualization of gene expression and with the demonstration of the potential of this approach to study the spatial and temporal regulation of gene expression in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new vectors described here are useful for monitoring differential gene expression in B. subtilus.
, in this work, we present new cloning vectors, based on the pDG1729 vector, for the expression of the cfp and yFP variants in B. subtili.
the new CFP and YPF variants are useful reporter proteins for the visualization of differential gene expression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of CFP and YPF fusions is a powerful tool for the study of gene regulation in B. subtili s.
the improved CFP and YPF variants, together with the new cloning vectors, provide the basis for the construction of a variety of reporter gene fusions in B. subtili s.

the use of CFP and YYP variants that have been modified to improve the production of the fluorescent proteins in B. subtili is a valuable tool in the analysis of the differential gene expression in this bacterium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N terminus of a protein plays an important role in its expression level in B. subtilus.
improved fluorescent protein production can be achieved by adding the N-terminal part from a B. subtilus protein to the N terminus of the fluorescent protein.
the production of fluorescent proteins in bacteria can be improved by extending the N-terminal part, which is a general strategy that should also apply to other fluorescent proteins.
